title: Sell Mineral Rights in Colstrip, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Colstrip, MT
metaDescription: Colstrip is Montana's coal-power hub, and the split between coal and oil-gas rights on your deed matters. A former operations engineer explains what to check before selling.
heroLead: Colstrip is coal country first, oil and gas country second, and I check which category your mineral deed actually covers before saying anything about value.
intro: Colstrip grew up around Western Energy's Rosebud Mine and the coal-fired power plant that still anchors the town's economy, one of the largest strip-mining operations in the state. That history shapes how mineral rights here get evaluated, because a lot of deeds in this area separate coal from oil, gas, and other minerals, sometimes reserved to different parties entirely.

sections.heading: Coal Rights Are Not the Same as Oil and Gas Rights
paragraphs: If your family's deed near Colstrip reserves coal separately, that interest is tied to a completely different value driver, surface coal mining leases and royalty structures, than any oil and gas interest you might also hold. I pull the actual severance language before assuming your mineral deed covers everything below the surface, because in this part of Rosebud County it often doesn't.

sections.heading: Oil and Gas Activity Around Colstrip
paragraphs: Beyond coal, Rosebud County has genuine coalbed methane history from the CBM development era of the late 1990s and 2000s, with wells targeting the Fort Union coal seams in areas near and around Colstrip. Much of that activity has matured into steady decline, though it represents more actual drilling history than most of the surrounding Powder River MT counties.

sections.heading: Evaluating a Colstrip-Area Interest
paragraphs: I start by confirming exactly what your deed reserves, coal, oil and gas, or both, then check current CBM well performance and payment history if applicable. Given the county's real production history here, this is a more substantive value conversation than in the quieter reservation-interior towns nearby, and I'll walk through the specifics with you directly.

faqs.question: Does my mineral deed near Colstrip include coal rights?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. Given Colstrip's coal mining history, many deeds in this area separate coal reservations from oil, gas, and other minerals. Check the original severance language at the Rosebud County Clerk and Recorder in Forsyth to see exactly what your deed covers.

faqs.question: Is there active coalbed methane production near Colstrip?
faqs.answer: There's real CBM history here from development in the late 1990s and 2000s, targeting the Fort Union coal seams. Much of it has matured into steady decline, but it's more substantial than in most of the surrounding area.

faqs.question: Who operates the coal mine near Colstrip?
faqs.answer: The Rosebud Mine has historically been operated by Western Energy Company, supplying the adjacent power plant. That's a separate business from any oil and gas leasing on the same or nearby land.
